mainTopic: Liability for carrying a vessel with food, and whether a living being carries itself (חי נושא את עצמו) on שבת
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about someone who carries food in a vessel and is liable 'even for the vessel.' רב אשי rejects the explanation that he was שוגג on the food and מזיד on the vessel. He explains instead that the person was שוגג on both and became aware of each at a different time, which depends on the dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's rule that carrying a living person on a bed is פטור, even for the bed. It asks whether this follows only רבי נתן, who holds that a living being carries itself (חי נושא את עצמו). רבא answers that even רבנן agree when a person is being carried, and they argue only about animals. A challenge from בן בתירא's permission to sell a horse is answered by limiting it to a horse that carries falcons. רבי יוחנן adds that רבי נתן agrees a tied-up (כפות) being does not carry itself, and Persian riders are shown not to count as כפות. Finally, the גמרא quotes the משנה about carrying a מת on a bed and begins a statement about רבי שמעון's exemption, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Unwitting about the food, intentional about the vessel
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier answer: the ברייתא's double liability is a case where the person was שוגג about the food and מזיד about the vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The case is] where he acted unknowingly regarding the food and on purpose regarding the vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an answer that began on the previous amud. It explains how a person carrying food in a vessel can be liable for both: he was שוגג on the food and מזיד on the vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that someone carrying food in a vessel is liable 'even for the vessel.' This answer explains the double liability through two different states of mind. For the food he brings a חטאת because he was שוגג. For the vessel he gets כרת because he was מזיד.

keyTerms.meaning: Acted unknowingly (שוגג), which obligates a חטאת
Acted on purpose (מזיד), which brings כרת or punishment

phrases.english: where he acted unknowingly regarding the food
phrases.notes: This is the second half of an answer begun earlier.

phrases.english: and acted on purpose regarding the vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁשָּׁגַג עַל הָאוֹכָלִין וְהֵזִיד עַל הַכְּלִי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It was unclear how one act of carrying can create two liabilities.
steps.terutzMaskana: The food is שוגג and the vessel is מזיד, so each carries its own liability.

steps.title: רב אשי objects: 'even for the vessel' means the same liability
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי argues that the wording 'אף על הכלי' implies the vessel's liability is the same kind as the food's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי challenged this: But it teaches 'even for the vessel'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the answer from step 1 based on the ברייתא's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'even' (אף) suggests the vessel is liable in exactly the same way as the food. If one is a חטאת and the other is כרת, the ברייתא would not say 'even.' So the שוגג/מזיד explanation does not fit the text.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches! (a challenge from the wording of a source)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi challenged it:
But it teaches "even for the vessel"!
phrases.notes: 'Even' implies the same type of liability.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי וְהָא אַף עַל הַכְּלִי קָתָנֵי
steps.kashyaTarget: The שוגג/מזיד explanation of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'אף' means equal liability, but the answer gives two different kinds of liability.

steps.title: רב אשי's case: unwitting on both, with separate awareness
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains the case as שוגג on both items, with separate moments of realization. Whether this creates two חטאות depends on the dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: For example, where he was unknowing about both this and that, and he found out [about one], and then found out [about the other]. And this is in the dispute of רבי יוחנן and רבי שמעון בן לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new explanation where both liabilities are the same kind, a חטאת. This fits the word 'even.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person was שוגג about both the food and the vessel. He then learned of each sin at a different time. Whether separate realizations split one act into two חטאות is the dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש quoted earlier in the sugya. The ברייתא follows the view that they do.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejects the old answer and brings a new one)
And then later became aware again

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, 'even for the vessel' means two equal חטאות. This works only according to the view that separate realizations (ידיעות) split the liability.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
for example, where he was unknowing about this and that,
and he found out, and then again found out,
phrases.notes: He learned about the food and the vessel at separate times.

phrases.english: and it is in the dispute of Rabbi Yochanan
and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי כְּגוֹן שֶׁשָּׁגַג בָּזֶה וּבָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's own challenge with a new case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two liabilities were different (חטאת and כרת).
steps.terutzMaskana: Both liabilities are חטאות, split by separate realizations, following one side of the רבי יוחנן/ריש לקיש dispute.

steps.title: The משנה: carrying a living person on a bed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: someone who carries out a living person on a bed is פטור, even for the bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] A living person on a bed: he is exempt even for the bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying the person is exempt, and the bed is treated as secondary (טפל) to him. So there is no liability for the bed either. The next step asks whose view this exemption follows.

phrases.english: [one who carries out] a living person on a bed
is exempt even for the bed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶת הַחַי בַּמִּטָּה פָּטוּר אַף עַל הַמִּטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: a quote from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying a living person on a bed is פטור, including for the bed.

steps.title: Does the משנה follow only רבי נתן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה follows רבי נתן, who exempts carrying live animals because 'a living being carries itself.' The חכמים make one liable even for live animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say the משנה is רבי נתן and not רבנן? As it was taught: One who carries out a domestic animal, wild animal, or bird into the public domain, whether alive or slaughtered, is liable. רבי נתן says: for slaughtered ones he is liable, and for live ones he is exempt, because a living being carries itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that our משנה matches only the minority view of רבי נתן. It brings a ברייתא to show the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן holds that a living creature helps carry itself (חי נושא את עצמו), so the carrier did not really carry it. The חכמים make one liable even for live animals. If the משנה exempts carrying a live person, it seems to follow only רבי נתן, which is a problem because the משנה should follow the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say (a suggestion the גמרא may reject)
As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: 'לימא' is only a suggestion. The גמרא usually rejects it right away, as רבא does in the next step.

phrases.english: Shall we say our mishnah is Rabbi Natan's view
and not the Rabbis'?
As it was taught: One who carries out a domestic animal, a wild animal, or a bird
into the public domain,
whether alive or slaughtered, is liable.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: עַל שְׁחוּטִין חַיָּיב
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says: for slaughtered ones he is liable,
and for live ones he is exempt,
because a living being carries itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי נָתָן הִיא וְלָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whose opinion the quoted משנה follows.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's exemption for carrying a live person
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only רבי נתן exempts carrying living beings. The חכמים make one liable, so the משנה seems to follow a minority view.

steps.title: רבא: even the חכמים agree about a living person
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the חכמים argue only about animals, which go limp and resist being carried. A living person helps carry himself, and even the חכמים agree to that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can even say it is רבנן. רבנן only argue with רבי נתן about animals and birds, which make themselves heavy to escape. But a living person, who carries himself, even רבנן agree.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends the משנה so that it matches the majority view too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals struggle and make themselves heavy to get free (משרבטי נפשייהו), so they do not help the carrier. A person cooperates and lightens his own load. So everyone agrees that carrying a live person is פטור, and the dispute is only about animals.

keyTerms.meaning: They only argue in this case
They make themselves limp and heavy to escape

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, everyone holds that a live person carries himself. The dispute between רבי נתן and the חכמים is only about animals.

phrases.english: Rava said: You can even say it is the Rabbis;
the Rabbis only argue
with Rabbi Natan
about domestic animals, wild animals, and birds,
which make themselves heavy [trying to escape];

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אָדָם חַי דְּנוֹשֵׂא אֶת עַצְמוֹ —
phrases.english: but a living person, who carries himself —
even the Rabbis agree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion that the משנה follows only רבי נתן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים disagree with חי נושא את עצמו in every case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים disagree only for animals. For a person, everyone agrees.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: why link בן בתירא only to רבי נתן?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן said that בן בתירא, who permits selling a horse to a non-Jew, holds the same as רבי נתן. If the חכמים also agree that a person carries himself, why single out רבי נתן?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said to רבא: But what we learned, 'בן בתירא permits a horse,' and it was taught, 'בן בתירא permits a horse because it does a labor for which one is not liable a חטאת,' and רבי יוחנן said, 'בן בתירא and רבי נתן said the same thing.' If you say רבנן only argue about animals because they make themselves heavy, why specifically בן בתירא and רבי נתן? You said even רבנן agree!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה challenges רבא using a statement of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן בתירא permits selling a riding horse because carrying a rider is not a מלאכה, since the person carries himself. רבי יוחנן ties this view to רבי נתן alone, which implies the חכמים disagree. But according to רבא, the חכמים agree about a person, so רבי יוחנן should not have limited it to רבי נתן.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who permits selling a horse to a non-Jew
Sin-offering, brought for a שוגג violation of a מלאכה
The same thing (they hold the same view)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרָבָא,
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said to Rava:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא דִּתְנַן: בֶּן בְּתִירָא מַתִּיר בַּסּוּס.
phrases.english: But what we learned: Ben Beteira permits [selling] a horse.
phrases.notes: This refers to selling work animals to non-Jews.

phrases.english: And it was taught: Ben Beteira permits a horse
because it does with it a labor
for which one is not liable a sin-offering,
and Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן בְּתִירָא וְרַבִּי נָתָן אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד.
phrases.english: Ben Beteira and Rabbi Natan said the same thing.
And if you say the Rabbis do not argue
with Rabbi Natan
except about domestic animals, wild animals, and birds
because they make themselves heavy,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אִירְיָא בֶּן בְּתִירָא וְרַבִּי נָתָן?
phrases.english: why specifically Ben Beteira and Rabbi Natan?
But you said even the Rabbis agree!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרָבָא וְהָא דִּתְנַן
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the חכמים agree a person carries himself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן linking בן בתירא only to רבי נתן implies the חכמים disagree even about a person riding.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן meant a horse used for carrying birds
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's link to רבי נתן refers to a horse that carries birds. That case depends on the animal dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יוחנן said it, it was about a horse designated for birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by narrowing what רבי יוחנן was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the horse carries live birds, the question is whether live birds carry themselves. That is exactly where רבי נתן and the חכמים disagree. So רבי יוחנן's comparison fits, and רבא's view about people remains standing.

keyTerms.meaning: When he said it (he meant a specific case)

phrases.english: When Rabbi Yochanan said it,
it was about a horse designated for birds.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּסוּס הַמְיוּחָד לְעוֹפוֹת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting a statement to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן was talking about a horse carrying a person.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was talking about a horse carrying birds, where the animal dispute applies.

steps.title: Is there really a horse just for birds?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether such a horse actually exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there such a thing as a horse designated for birds?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks whether the case from step 8 is realistic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An answer based on an imaginary case would be weak. So the גמרא asks whether a horse used only for carrying birds really exists.

keyTerms.meaning: And is there really such a thing?

phrases.english: And is there a horse designated for birds?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the case in step 8 is realistic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a horse dedicated to carrying birds exists in reality

steps.title: Yes, the falconers' horse
steps.stepSummary: Yes. Hunters use horses to carry their falcons.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, there is: that of the falconers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that such horses really exist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hunters who use birds keep horses for carrying them. So step 8's answer is based on a real case.

phrases.english: Yes, there is: that of the falconers.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Falconers have horses designated for carrying birds.

steps.title: רבי נתן agrees about a tied-up person
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that even רבי נתן agrees that a bound (כפות) person or animal does not carry itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: And רבי נתן agrees regarding one who is tied up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement that limits the rule חי נושא את עצמו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that a living being carries itself only works if it can help. A tied-up being cannot lighten its load, so it is like a dead weight. Carrying it would make one liable even according to רבי נתן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
And Rabbi Natan agrees regarding one who is tied up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי נָתָן בְּכָפוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to רבי נתן's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bound being does not carry itself, so carrying it makes one liable even according to רבי נתן.

steps.title: The Persians are like bound people, yet the horse is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנה points out that Persian horsemen are like כפות, yet רבי יוחנן still said that בן בתירא and רבי נתן agree to permit selling horses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנה said to אביי: But these Persians are considered like bound people, and רבי יוחנן said that בן בתירא and רבי נתן said the same thing!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר מתנה challenges the rule about כפות from step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Persian riders in heavy armor seem unable to help carry themselves, which makes them like a bound person. Then the horse would be carrying a real load, so selling it should be forbidden. Yet בן בתירא permits selling a horse, and רבי יוחנן said that רבי נתן holds the same view, even though רבי נתן agrees about a כפות.

keyTerms.meaning: They are like people who are bound

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana said to Abaye:
But these Persians
are like people who are tied up,
and [yet] Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן בְּתִירָא וְרַבִּי נָתָן אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד!
phrases.english: Ben Beteira and Rabbi Natan said the same thing!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה לְאַבָּיֵי וְהָא הָנֵי פָּרְסָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the כפות rule from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that רבי נתן agrees about a כפות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Persian riders are like כפות, so the horse should count as carrying them. Yet the horse is permitted.

steps.title: The Persians ride out of arrogance
steps.stepSummary: Persians are not truly unable to walk. Their pride is what keeps them on horseback.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is arrogance that holds them [on the horse].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the Persians are not really like bound people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כפות physically cannot help carry himself. The Persians can walk and help, but they choose to ride because of pride. So they still carry themselves, and the horse is permitted.

phrases.english: There, it is arrogance
that holds them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם רָמוּת רוּחָא הוּא דְּנָקֵיט לְהוּ
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Persian riders are physically unable to walk, like a כפות.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are able to walk. Pride, not inability, keeps them riding.

steps.title: Proof: the officer who ran three parasangs
steps.stepSummary: A Persian officer at whom the king was angry ran three פרסאות on foot. This shows Persians can walk.
steps.simpleTranslation: For that officer at whom the king was angry ran three parasangs on his feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to prove the answer in step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a Persian officer could run three פרסאות on foot, Persians are clearly not physically bound. This supports the claim that they ride from pride, so the rule חי נושא את עצמו still applies to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Parasangs (פרסאות), a large unit of distance

steps.whatToRemember: חי נושא את עצמו applies whenever the living being is able to help carry itself. It does not apply to a truly bound being. Persians are able, so the rule applies to them.

phrases.english: For that [Persian] officer
at whom the king was angry
ran three parasangs on his feet.

steps.raayaObject: The claim that Persians can walk and are not like a כפות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the officer who ran three פרסאות on foot

steps.title: The next case of the משנה: a corpse on a bed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: carrying out a מת on a bed makes one חייב, and so does carrying a כזית of a מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one who carries out a dead body on a bed is liable. The same is true of one who carries out an olive-sized piece of a dead body, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה and quotes it. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the משנה taught that a living person carried on a bed is פטור, because a living person helps carry himself. A מת cannot help carry itself, so the first opinion of the משנה rules that carrying it is a real act of carrying and one is חייב. The "וכו׳" points to the rest of the משנה, including רבי שמעון's view that one is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: A bed, here a bier used to carry the body
Liable, meaning he has done a forbidden מלאכה on שבת
An olive-sized amount, the minimum size that counts
"Etc.", meaning the quote continues in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the live person on a bed from earlier. A חי is פטור because he carries himself. A מת cannot do that, so the first opinion says one is חייב.

phrases.english: [One who carries out] a corpse on a bed is liable
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה. Compare it with a live person on a bed, where he's exempt.

phrases.english: and similarly an olive-bulk of a corpse, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: a כזית of a נבלה, a lentil-bulk of a שרץ, and רבי שמעון exempts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶת הַמֵּת בַּמִּטָּה חַיָּיב וְכֵן כְּזַיִת מִן הַמֵּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of horses, Persians and כפות, and moves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying a מת on a bed, or a כזית of a מת, makes one חייב according to the first opinion of the משנה. רבי שמעון exempts.

steps.title: Two chains of tradition begin explaining רבי שמעון's exemption
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quoting רבי יוחנן, and רב יוסף quoting ריש לקיש, both begin to explain how far רבי שמעון's פטור goes. The statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן, and רב יוסף said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: רבי שמעון would exempt...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two matching traditions that are about to define the reach of רבי שמעון's exemption. The sentence is cut off here and finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש are quoted saying the same thing, which gives the statement extra weight. The phrase "פוטר היה רבי שמעון" tells us they are going to expand on the משנה's simple words "ורבי שמעון פוטר". They will show that his exemption applies even in a case we might have thought he would agree is חייב. That point is completed on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempts, rules that one is not liable
The תנא in the משנה who exempts one who carries out a מת
ריש לקיש, the famous אמורא and study partner of רבי יוחנן
An אמורא who often reports teachings of רבי יוחנן

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different people named שמעון here. רבי שמעון is the תנא in the משנה whose view is being explained. רבי שמעון בן לקיש (ריש לקיש) is a later אמורא who is reporting that explanation.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said,
phrases.notes: This is the first line of rabbis passing the statement down.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: and Rav Yosef said that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
phrases.notes: A second line of rabbis, passing down the same statement.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon would deem exempt
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud and defines the scope of the exemption.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ פּוֹטֵר הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the רבי שמעון part of the משנה line just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: (Incomplete on this amud.) רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both report how widely רבי שמעון applied his exemption for carrying a מת.
